english: The sum $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}\,4}{n(n+1)(n+2)}$ can be written as $\alpha\log_e2+\beta$, where $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers. Then the value of $\alpha\beta$ is ______.
hindi: योग $\displaystyle\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n+1}\,4}{n(n+1)(n+2)}$ को $\alpha\log_e2+\beta$ के रूप में लिखा जा सकता है, जहाँ $\alpha$ तथा $\beta$ पूर्णांक हैं। तब $\alpha\beta$ का मान ______ है।
solution_full: Partial fractions: $\dfrac{4}{n(n+1)(n+2)}=\dfrac{2}{n}-\dfrac{4}{n+1}+\dfrac{2}{n+2}$ (the weights $1,-2,1$ that make the non-alternating series telescope).
All three series converge, so the given sum is $2\log_e2-4(1-\log_e2)+2\left(\log_e2-\dfrac12\right)=8\log_e2-5$.
Numerically $8\log_e2-5\approx0.5452$, which agrees with the partial sums.
If $\alpha\log_e2+\beta=8\log_e2-5$ with integers $\alpha,\beta$ and $\alpha\neq8$, then $\log_e2$ would be rational, which is false. So $\alpha=8$, $\beta=-5$, and $\alpha\beta=-40$.
originality_note: New: the familiar telescoping fraction 1/(n(n+1)(n+2)) is given alternating signs, so it no longer telescopes; its partial-fraction pieces become three shifted copies of the series for log_e 2 (way 5: linear-denominator decomposition linked with the logarithmic series). Closest known: 'sum 1/(n(n+1)(n+2)) = 1/4' and 'sum (-1)^{n+1}/(n(n+1)) = 2 log 2 - 1'. Different because: the cubic denominator with alternation needs three index shifts of log 2 and gives a mixed answer 8 log 2 - 5.
